purpose: Cross-check JANUS autolearning architecture recommendations against recent public research without converting papers into automatic training truth.

sources.title: Revisiting Replay and Gradient Alignment for Continual Pre-Training of Large Language Models
sources.venue: Proceedings of The 4th Conference on Lifelong Learning Agents, PMLR 330
sources.finding: Across large continual-pretraining experiments, replay and gradient alignment improve stability under distribution shift; small replay rates can be an efficient use of compute.
sources.janus_translation: Supports bounded replay as a candidate anti-forgetting mechanism, not unrestricted replay. JANUS still requires verifier/provenance eligibility and a separate holdout.

sources.title: How Memory Management Impacts LLM Agents: An Empirical Study of Experience-Following Behavior
sources.finding: Agent behavior can strongly follow retrieved experiences; poor or misaligned experiences can propagate errors. Future task evaluations can provide quality signals for stored memory.
sources.janus_translation: Strong support for R2 verifier-stratified replay: a past success must carry explicit local verifier identity, target context and provenance before it can influence future decisions.

sources.title: Contextual Experience Replay for Self-Improvement of Language Agents
sources.finding: A dynamic memory buffer of past environment experiences can improve later agent behavior without parameter training when relevant experiences are retrieved contextually.
sources.janus_translation: Supports separating contextual replay from gradient updates. JANUS can first use verified outcomes as bounded selector/context priors before considering any parameter-level feedback.

sources.title: Towards Autonomous Memory Agents
sources.finding: Proposes memory agents that actively acquire, validate and curate knowledge using a cascade from cheap signals toward tool-verified research and expert feedback when uncertainty warrants it.
sources.janus_translation: Supports R6 layered research ingestion and uncertainty-driven evidence acquisition: DISCOVERY -> CORROBORATED -> TRAINING_ELIGIBLE.

sources.title: Audited Skill-Graph Self-Improvement for Agentic LLMs via Verifiable Rewards, Experience Synthesis, and Continual Memory
sources.finding: Frames self-improvement as accumulation of auditable skills promoted after verifier-backed replay and contract checks, with reconstructible evidence for learning signals.
sources.janus_translation: Conceptually aligns with proposal -> target-local VERIFY -> sealed receipt -> bounded learning, while JANUS keeps its own independent authority and provenance contracts.

sources.title: Self-Improvements in Modern Agentic Systems: A Survey
sources.finding: Organizes self-improvement by update target and feedback signal, emphasizing controllable adaptation across model parameters and operational scaffolds.
sources.janus_translation: Supports evaluating JANUS as both a weight-learning system and a scaffold-learning system; improvements to memory, verifier routing and proposal policy should be measured separately from checkpoint training.

sources.title: Continual Learning Bench 1.0
sources.finding: Evaluates systems on dependent task sequences where systems are expected to change during evaluation and performance depends on use of prior experience.
sources.janus_translation: Supports a future JANUS frozen sequential benchmark in addition to token-level loss: test whether verified prior experience improves later bounded tasks without increasing unsafe action or reducing abstention quality.

new_candidate.title: Frozen sequential retention benchmark
new_candidate.purpose: Measure whether JANUS uses verified experience to improve later tasks while retaining earlier capabilities, rather than relying only on language-model loss.
